summary: Soundness proof blocked by two implementation bugs: (1) isIntuitionisticallyClosed missing complementary-pair closure check (p→p returns open), (2) intTImpRule persistence over-fires at sibling worlds via Nat ordering (invalid formula ((¬p)→q)∨(p→r) incorrectly closes). Both verified by #eval. Sorry cannot be filled until implementation is fixed.
blockers: BUG 1: isIntuitionisticallyClosed only checks T(⊥), missing T(φ)/F(φ) complementary pair closure. Consequence: known tautologies like p→p and S-combinator return .openBranch. Fix: add Branch.hasContradiction check to IntuitionisticClosure.

BUG 2: intTImpRule (Rules.lean:129) uses Nat ordering (filter (· ≥ w)) as accessibility proxy. This fires T-implications at sibling worlds that are NOT accessible in the Kripke model. Consequence: ((p→⊥)→q)∨(p→r) incorrectly closes (T(⊥) added at sibling via T(p→⊥,1) + T(p,2)). Fix: track actual parent-child accessibility in expansion state, or restrict intTImpRule to only fire at labels created as descendants.

bug1_closure.issue: Only checks T(⊥), should also check Branch.hasContradiction
bug1_closure.fix: Add || Branch.hasContradiction b to the definition

bug2_persistence.issue: Uses (· ≥ w) Nat filter as accessibility proxy, but Nat ordering does not match tree-shaped Kripke accessibility for sibling worlds
bug2_persistence.counterexample: ((p→⊥)→q)∨(p→r) incorrectly closes via T(p→⊥,1) firing at sibling world 2
bug2_persistence.fix: Track parent-child relationships in expansion state and restrict intTImpRule to fire only along actual accessibility paths
